problems.issue: Defining skeletal features are absent from simulated biology: increased long-bone density is 0% and cortical thickening 2%, versus 92% and 83% reported in R1-train. Diaphyseal undertubulation alone does not capture this sclerosing bone dysplasia.

Hallmark findings are substantially underreported: anemia 44%, diaphyseal undertubulation 43%, diaphyseal dysplasia 9%, and thrombocytopenia 7%, versus 83%, 92%, 83%, and 58% in R1-train. This weakens the characteristic combination of skeletal disease and cytopenias.

Generic skeletal and immune terms displace diagnostic findings, while examples introduce misleading phenotypes. Record 1 suggests a dysmorphic developmental syndrome; record 2 includes myeloid leukemia without characteristic sclerosis or anemia; record 3 includes cleft palate and increased nuchal translucency. These are not established defining features of TBXAS1 disease and collectively create substantial diagnostic noise.

summary: Age and sex distributions are plausible, but missing osteosclerosis and cortical thickening, weak hallmark reporting, and unrelated example findings make the simulated patients clinically implausible.
